The average cat is supposed to weigh between 9 and 12 pounds, maybe up to 15 if it's a big cat like a Maine Coon or similar breed. This cat weighs nearly 3 times what he should, poor thing. Obese pets get all the same problems that obese humans do; joint pain, cardiovascular problems, breathing issues, etc.

We don't use BMI in cats, we use this chart or a similar one to generate a body condition score. As you can see, this cat is obese - I would even say super obese. That is not normal for a cat, the only way he got like that was by consuming too many calories.

He even had stretches — once after a fight with a feral cat — where he barely ate for several weeks. Still, nothing reduced the size of the obese feline.

This is complete bullshit, and I'll tell you why. If a cat goes even 48 hours without eating and then starts eating again, they go through a very severe form of refeeding syndrome, though it's not called that in cats. They have very sensitive livers, so going without food for even a short length of time and then being fed too much too quickly (so even going from nothing back to their normal diet) can cause a very severe form of fatty liver disease, which can be fatal. Also, CICO is the same for animals as it is for humans, so there's no way this cat went "several weeks" without eating barely anything.

"We've tried everything," she said, attributing his girth to a slow metabolism.

I mentioned this in a few comment replies, but here it is again: cats don't often end up with a "slow metabolism". Hypothyroidism in cats is extremely, extremely rare. It is far more likely for a cat to develop hyperthyroidism, in which the cat produces too much T3 and T4 and its metabolism is actually sped up.

Also, cats are more susceptible to Type 2 diabetes than dogs. Especially senior cats (any cat 7 years or older is considered a "senior" in the veterinary world). So it's very likely this cat's pancreas will crap out even faster because of his weight, and he'll be getting insulin injections for the rest of his short life.
